clue.text: Coming to river divers appear bold

parts.note: an advent is an arrival or coming
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire, a crossword regular
divers is an old word for various or several, so it means some

explanation.surface: Divers emerging at a river look daring as they arrive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'divers' is not people diving but the archaic adjective meaning various, hence SOME.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone daring enough to take risks is venturesome, hence bold.

clue.text: In heaven, raised in a previous passage

parts.note: heaven is thought of as up above
to raise a subject is to mention it

explanation.surface: Something exalted in heaven is cited in an earlier section of text.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrase describing what was referred to earlier in a document, in a prior paragraph.

clue.text: He helps to establish civic archives

indicators.note: the words civic archives help make up the run, which sits within them

explanation.surface: A man assists in founding a town's records office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He' is the whole definition: a clergyman. The run sits across 'civic' and 'archives'.
explanation.definitionFit: A vicar is a parish priest, traditionally a man, so the pronoun stands for him.

clue.text: One way to go for pole position

definitions.text: One way to go for pole position

parts.words: One way to go for pole position
parts.note: pole position suggests motor racing, but here it means the position of the North Pole, and a direction of travel to reach it

explanation.surface: A racing driver's tactic for securing the front of the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Heading towards the North Pole is travelling in the direction of north.

clue.text: Fabulous supporter up in arms

parts.note: fabulous means mythical, a supporter is a heraldic figure holding up a shield, and arms are a coat of arms rather than weapons or anger

explanation.surface: A wonderful backer who is angry and ready to fight.
explanation.walkthrough: In the British royal coat of arms the shield is held up by a lion and a mythical one-horned horse.
explanation.definitionFit: The mythical one-horned beast stands as a heraldic supporter on the royal coat of arms.

clue.text: Two holding hands work hard to join on

parts.note: in bridge the four hands are North, South, East and West, so two players' hands give E and N
to graft is to toil, British slang

explanation.surface: Two people hand in hand labour hard to unite.
explanation.definitionFit: To engraft is to graft or fix one thing onto another, attaching it.

clue.text: Secret police origins of old guard punch-ups

indicators.note: the origins of words are their opening letters, taken from the three words that follow

explanation.surface: Secret police started out as old-guard thugs fond of brawls.
explanation.definitionFit: The OGPU was the Soviet state security service of the 1920s and 30s.

clue.text: Somehow gets eager for the gift of Spring?

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters of gets eager are arranged in some other way

explanation.surface: Someone grows keen for a springtime present.
explanation.definitionFit: A chocolate treat traditionally given at the spring festival celebrating the Resurrection.

clue.text: Youth of Abydos such a devotee

definitions.text: Youth of Abydos such a devotee

parts.words: Youth of Abydos such a devotee
parts.note: in Greek legend Leander of Abydos swam the Hellespont nightly to visit his beloved, the priestess named Hero

explanation.surface: A young man from an ancient city was a great fan.
explanation.walkthrough: The general term for an idoliser is read literally: Leander was devoted to a woman called Hero.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who idolises another; Leander literally adored a woman called Hero.

clue.text: Commanding figure with dog-collar appearing

parts.note: OC is the military abbreviation for officer commanding
a cur is a mongrel dog
a ring round the neck acts as a collar

explanation.surface: A commanding officer turns up wearing a clerical collar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dog-collar' looks like a priest's collar but splits into dog and collar.
explanation.definitionFit: Something occurring is happening or turning up, as in showing up.

clue.text: Beat with stick?

definitions.meaning: to stick paper on a wall is to glue it up

explanation.surface: Hitting someone with a cane.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrash soundly in slang; also to glue, as with wallpaper adhesive.

clue.text: World terminal

explanation.surface: An airport terminal serving the globe.
explanation.definitionFit: Our planet, and in electrics the ground connection terminal.

clue.text: The ground is in shape

definitions.meaning: a cricket ground in south London

explanation.surface: The land has a definite form.
explanation.definitionFit: THE OVAL is a London cricket ground; also an egg-like elliptical figure.

clue.text: Love in a Cold Climate?

parts.note: the title of Nancy Mitford's novel, read as tennis love, meaning nil, in a freezing climate where the thermometer reads nil degrees

explanation.surface: A reference to Nancy Mitford's novel about romance among the English aristocracy.
explanation.definitionFit: Love means nil in tennis scoring, and a cold climate sits at nought degrees Celsius.

clue.text: Is the island under India? it can't be separated

indicators.note: in a down clue a piece under another is written after it

parts.note: Crete is the Greek island

explanation.surface: A question about where an island lies relative to India.
explanation.definitionFit: Indiscrete is a rare word meaning not divided into distinct parts, hence inseparable.

clue.text: Justify former simple alliance

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
plain means simple or unadorned

explanation.surface: Defending a past alliance that was straightforward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'alliance' only links the two pieces, as the joining of EX to PLAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: To explain one's conduct is to account for it, giving reasons that warrant it.

clue.text: Lawless like the band from Penzance

definitions.meaning: acting outside the law, like a buccaneer
Gilbert and Sullivan's comic opera The Pirates of Penzance features a band of sea robbers

explanation.surface: A Cornish band of musicians behaving lawlessly.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to sea robbers, who are lawless, as in Gilbert and Sullivan's opera set in Cornwall.

clue.text: Mixed fruit to put round cake perhaps

indicators.note: the word to is put round the cake, enclosing it

parts.note: angel cake is a light sponge, so angel can stand for a cake by example

explanation.surface: A recipe instruction to place fruit around a cake.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangelo is a hybrid citrus, a cross between tangerine and pomelo.

clue.text: Deals I entered into cause angry words

indicators.note: I has gone into the word for deals, sitting within it

parts.note: trades are business deals

explanation.surface: A card game with I involved provokes heated arguments.
explanation.definitionFit: Tirades are long, furious speeches of denunciation.

clue.text: Plug for the locum tenens

parts.note: a locum tenens is a stand-in doctor or priest, a temporary fill-in, just as a plug fills a hole until a proper fix

explanation.surface: Promoting the stand-in doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: A temporary substitute filling a vacancy, like a locum covering for an absent doctor.

clue.text: Creator of lines crossing the Thames?

definitions.meaning: Robert ... was Poet Laureate, a creator of lines of verse
the river through London is spanned by many such structures

explanation.surface: Someone who draws lines across London's river.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Bridges the poet, and structures spanning rivers such as the Thames.

clue.text: Sign for what is left

definitions.meaning: Libra, the zodiac sign, is represented by scales
the remainder, as in a bank statement's amount left over

explanation.surface: A notice saying what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: Libra's symbol is a pair of weighing scales; also the remainder owed or left.

clue.text: Unseemly word spoken in court

definitions.meaning: a witness swears a solemn promise to tell the truth

explanation.surface: Someone swears in a courtroom.
explanation.definitionFit: A curse is a swear word; also the sworn promise a witness makes.

clue.text: Jack awaits arrival of such a vessel

definitions.text: Jack awaits arrival of such a vessel

parts.words: Jack awaits arrival of such a vessel
parts.note: Jack looks like a sailor awaiting a ship, but in lawn ... the jack is the small target ball the woods roll up to

explanation.surface: A sailor waits for his ship to come in.
explanation.definitionFit: In lawn bowls each wood rolled towards the jack is called this, also a word for a basin or dish.

clue.text: Island where many spend almost a month

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, taken as many

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the month is left off

parts.note: April is a month

explanation.surface: An island where lots of people holiday for nearly a month.
explanation.definitionFit: Capri is an Italian island in the Bay of Naples.

clue.text: Russian physicist told to depart quickly

indicators.note: told signals a word said out loud, its sound standing for the entry

parts.note: to pop off is to leave in a hurry

explanation.surface: A Russian scientist is ordered to leave in a hurry.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexander Popov was a Russian pioneer of radio, so a physicist.

clue.text: Sign showing how the staff works

definitions.text: Sign showing how the staff works

parts.words: Sign showing how the staff works
parts.note: the staff here is the musical stave, and the symbol at its start fixes the pitch of its lines

explanation.surface: A notice explaining how employees operate.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical symbol at the start of a stave indicating which pitches the lines represent.

clue.text: From forty we hear better?

indicators.note: we hear signals the letters are judged by sound

parts.note: from is EX, and forty is XL in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Asking whether people over forty are improving.
explanation.definitionFit: To excel is to surpass, so to better as a verb.

clue.text: Colour and music and something to drink

parts.note: ginger is a reddish-orange colour
pop is popular music

explanation.surface: A list of a colour, a type of music and a beverage.
explanation.definitionFit: A fizzy soft drink flavoured with root spice, an old British name for ginger beer.

clue.text: This club is a time-saver.

parts.note: club as a weapon, a cosh; and time as a prison term, which a life sentence would cover, so the saver is a preserver of a life

explanation.surface: A society promising to save its members time.
explanation.definitionFit: A short weighted cudgel carried for self-defence; also a flotation ring saving one from drowning.
